body:
The 2º option not opening at all does indeed looks like its because the new node was not added into the SceneTree. Since the Android backend seems to default to Godot's builtin dialog, then there is this requirement for the dialog to be displayed.

From the code, it seems this is because the Android backend does not support `FEATURE_NATIVE_DIALOG_FILE_EXTRA`, which is what is needed for a file dialog to open resources only in `res://`/`user://` paths.

> [@Yobbolita](https://github.com/Yobbolita) This is an expected behaviour. Native file dialog on Android can only access the filesystem, it is documented here https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_filedialog.html#class-filedialog-property-use-native-dialog
> 
> > Note: On Android, it is only supported when using [ACCESS_FILESYSTEM](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_filedialog.html#class-filedialog-constant-access-filesystem). For access mode [ACCESS_RESOURCES](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_filedialog.html#class-filedialog-constant-access-resources) and [ACCESS_USERDATA](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/classes/class_filedialog.html#class-filedialog-constant-access-userdata), the system will fall back to custom FileDialog.
> 
> In method 1, You haven't set the access mode to `ACCESS_FILESYSTEM`, so it's falling back to Godot's custom FileDialog. Same in method 2, but here nothing happens because you haven't added the node to scene tree.

Tested on the same Android 16, can confirm that changing the access mode in the FileDialog works for method 1.

Problem Solved.
